digester-gas-production.formula: VS_destroyed = VS_fed x reduction/100; gas = VS_destroyed x yield; methane = gas x methane_pct/100; energy = methane x 960 BTU/ft^3.
digester-gas-production.edition: Anaerobic digester gas production (WEF; university operator courses), by name.
digester-gas-production.freeAccess: The digester-gas production relation and its typical yields are public wastewater-operations results; the digester monitoring and the operator govern.
digester-gas-production.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
digester-gas-production.editionNote: The yield (12-18 ft^3/lb VS destroyed, default 15) and the methane fraction (~65%) depend on the feed and temperature - a digester-gas analysis governs the real values. The energy counts the methane heating value only (~960 BTU/ft^3); the CO2 fraction carries none. The estimate assumes steady mesophilic operation. The digester monitoring and the operator of record govern - a planning estimate, not a metered gas measurement.

assumptions.name: Gas yield
assumptions.value: 12-18 ft^3 digester gas per lb VS destroyed (default 15); feed- and temperature-dependent

assumptions.name: Methane and energy
assumptions.value: gas is ~65% methane; recoverable energy is methane x ~960 BTU/ft^3 (the CO2 carries none)

manure-nutrient-application.formula: avail_N_per_ton = total_N x availability%; rate = crop_N_need / avail_N_per_ton; P2O5_applied = rate x P2O5/ton; K2O_applied = rate x K2O/ton.
manure-nutrient-application.edition: Nitrogen-based manure application rate and the co-applied P/K, per USDA NRCS Code 590 (Nutrient Management), by name.
manure-nutrient-application.freeAccess: The N-based rate and the co-applied nutrient arithmetic follow the public USDA NRCS Code 590 nutrient-management method.
manure-nutrient-application.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
manure-nutrient-application.editionNote: The manure application rate set by the nitrogen need: the available N per ton = the manure's total N x the first-year availability (mineralization) factor, and the rate = the crop N requirement / the available N per ton. Meeting the N need also delivers whatever P2O5 and K2O the manure carries, and because manure is nitrogen-poor relative to phosphorus, an N-based rate usually over-applies P - the reason a nutrient-management plan switches to a P-based rate on high-phosphorus soils. This reports the P2O5 and K2O delivered so the over-application is visible (see also manure-application-rate for the rate alone). A planning aid; a manure test, the soil test, and the NRCS Code 590 nutrient-management plan govern.

assumptions.name: Available N
assumptions.value: total N x first-year availability; rate = crop N need / available N

assumptions.name: Co-applied P/K
assumptions.value: P2O5 and K2O = rate x their content per ton

assumptions.name: P over-application
assumptions.value: an N-based rate usually over-applies phosphorus; the plan governs

gear-mph-rpm.formula: MPH = RPM * pi * dia(in) * 60 / (trans * axle * 63,360); inverse for RPM; revs/mile = 63,360 / (pi * dia).
gear-mph-rpm.edition: Classical drivetrain kinematics; SAE J267 metric tire-size convention for decoding a tire code to diameter, by name.
gear-mph-rpm.freeAccess: Pure geometry, public; consistent with the tire-gearing tile.
gear-mph-rpm.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
gear-mph-rpm.editionNote: Single-identity (geometric no-slip speed); ignores tire and torque-converter slip.

assumptions.name: No slip
assumptions.value: geometric speed ignores tire and torque-converter slip

voltage-imbalance.formula: % imbalance = max deviation from average / average × 100; NEMA MG 1 derating table (2/5/12/18/25% HP at 1-5%), linearly interpolated from 0% upward.
voltage-imbalance.freeAccess: NEMA standards licensed; principles free in IEEE-USA outreach.
voltage-imbalance.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed electrician govern. Verify against the NEC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.

assumptions.name: Trip threshold
assumptions.value: > 5% halts the motor (engineering practice)

transformer-kva-sizing.formula: Total connected kVA = Σ load_i; required kVA = connected × (1 + reserve%). Recommended size from the ANSI/IEEE C57 standard step series (three-phase 15 / 30 / 45 / 75 / 112.5 / 150 / 225 / 300 / 500 / 750 / 1000; single-phase 10 / 15 / 25 / 37.5 / 50 / 75 / 100 / 167 / 250 / 333 / 500). FLA = kVA × 1000 / (V × √phases).
transformer-kva-sizing.edition: ANSI/IEEE C57 standard kVA step series by name; NEC 2023 (NFPA 70). Article 450 (Transformers).
transformer-kva-sizing.freeAccess: Free read-only access at nfpa.org/freeaccess. ANSI/IEEE C57 licensed; step-series values free in carrier engineering literature.
transformer-kva-sizing.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed electrician govern. Verify against the NEC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
transformer-kva-sizing.editionNote: Editions available: bundled values follow NEC 2023. NEC 2026 is the current published edition; jurisdictions on NEC 2017 / 2020 / 2023 / 2026 use slightly different ambient corrections and ampacity ranges; verify the edition adopted by your AHJ. Step series stable across NEC editions (ANSI/IEEE C57 governs the manufacturer step ladder).

assumptions.name: Default future-growth reserve
assumptions.value: 25% unless user supplies
assumptions.source: engineering practice for general-purpose service transformers

outdoor-air-ventilation.formula: Vbz = Rp * Pz + Ra * Az. Voz = Vbz / E_z. Per-person and per-area ratios surface the design density.
outdoor-air-ventilation.edition: ASHRAE 62.1-2022 §6.2.2.1 (single-zone breathing-zone procedure). AHJ-adopted edition governs.
outdoor-air-ventilation.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed mechanical contractor govern. ACCA Manual J / D / S supersede rules of thumb.
outdoor-air-ventilation.editionNote: ASHRAE 62.1 Table 6-1 occupancy categories are NOT bundled; user enters Rp and Ra from the AHJ-adopted edition.

assumptions.name: Rp / Ra
assumptions.value: user-supplied; placeholder presets for office / classroom / retail are starting points only

assumptions.name: E_z default
assumptions.value: 1.0 (ceiling supply with ceiling return)

assumptions.name: E_z range
assumptions.value: 0.5 to 1.2 typical

humidifier-capacity.formula: Moisture addition (lb/hr) = 60 × CFM × rho × (W_target − W_entering); W = 0.621945 × Pw / (P − Pw) with Pw = RH × Pws(T_db) and P the altitude-corrected pressure. Daily water = lb/hr × 24 / 8.34. Latent load = addition × 1061 BTU/lb.
humidifier-capacity.freeAccess: ASHRAE Handbook TOC free at ashrae.org; full handbook licensed.
humidifier-capacity.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed mechanical contractor govern. ACCA Manual J / D / S supersede rules of thumb.
humidifier-capacity.editionNote: Saturation vapor pressure by the Magnus form; air density from the ideal-gas law at the standard-atmosphere altitude pressure. AHJ and the manufacturer's published humidifier capacity govern actual delivery.

assumptions.name: Latent heat of vaporization
assumptions.value: 1061 BTU/lb (near room temperature)

assumptions.name: Water density
assumptions.value: 8.34 lb/gal

gas-pipe-sizing.formula: IFGC Equation 4-1 (low pressure, under 1.5 psi), D = Q^0.381 / (19.17 (dH / (Cr L))^0.206), solved for Q -- the relation Tables 402.4(1)-(36) are generated from -- sizing a SINGLE run of the entered length: it picks the smallest listed diameter whose capacity meets the load. Cr 0.6094 natural gas, 1.2462 undiluted propane. This is a single-segment estimate, NOT the full IFGC 2021 Section 402.4 / Tables 402.4(1)-(36) longest-length network method; a multi-branch system is sized on the single longest run to the most remote appliance, which the AHJ and the tables govern.
gas-pipe-sizing.edition: IFGC 2021 (International Fuel Gas Code) / NFPA 54. Section 402.4 and capacity tables.
gas-pipe-sizing.freeAccess: Free read-only access at codes.iccsafe.org. NFPA 54: Free read-only access at nfpa.org/freeaccess.
gas-pipe-sizing.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed plumber / gas fitter govern. Verify against the IPC / IFGC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
gas-pipe-sizing.editionNote: Editions available: bundled values follow IFGC 2021 / NFPA 54-2021. IFGC 2027 is the current published edition and 2024 preceded it; jurisdictions on any of these differ at the margins; verify the edition adopted by your AHJ.

assumptions.name: Pressure-drop allowance
assumptions.value: 0.5 in WC (low-pressure) / 1.0 psig (medium-pressure) unless user supplies

assumptions.name: Gas factor Cr
assumptions.value: 0.6094 natural gas (SG 0.60) / 1.2462 undiluted propane (SG 1.52)

septic-pumpout-interval.formula: Allowed accumulation = tank volume x fill fraction; years between pump-outs = allowed accumulation / (occupants x accumulation per person per year).
septic-pumpout-interval.edition: USEPA Onsite Wastewater Treatment Systems Manual (EPA/625/R-00/008); university onsite-wastewater extension pumping-frequency guidance, by name.
septic-pumpout-interval.freeAccess: Free at epa.gov/septic. Extension pumping-frequency tables free on land-grant university extension sites.
septic-pumpout-interval.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed plumber / gas fitter govern. Verify against the IPC / IFGC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
septic-pumpout-interval.editionNote: Single-edition (EPA manual + extension pumping-frequency guidance, refreshed at build time).

assumptions.name: Default accumulation
assumptions.value: 30 gal per person per year of net sludge + scum (a garbage disposal roughly doubles it); editable

assumptions.name: Default fill fraction
assumptions.value: 0.33 of the tank before pumping; editable

assumptions.name: Measurement governs
assumptions.value: a sludge-judge or core measurement of actual sludge and scum depth governs; never let sludge reach the outlet baffle; many states set a mandatory interval that overrides any estimate

beverage-co2-duration.formula: kegs_per_cylinder = cylinder_lb / lb_co2_per_keg; days_of_supply = kegs_per_cylinder / kegs_per_day; changeout_kegs = kegs_per_cylinder x (1 - reserve_fraction); changeout_days = changeout_kegs / kegs_per_day.
beverage-co2-duration.edition: Per-keg gas consumption of a draft system from public draft-beer engineering practice, for which the Brewers Association Draught Beer Quality Manual is the standard reference, by name; a cylinder scale and the gas supplier's measured consumption govern.
beverage-co2-duration.freeAccess: The duration arithmetic is division on the bar's own numbers: cylinder weight, pounds of CO2 per keg for the system type, kegs dispensed per day, and the reserve the operator wants.
beverage-co2-duration.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
beverage-co2-duration.editionNote: CO2 leaves a beverage cylinder two ways. It pushes beer out of the keg, and it stays dissolved in the beer that leaves. Both scale with the volume dispensed rather than with the number of taps, which is why a two-tap bar and a twelve-tap bar pouring the same number of kegs in a year use the same gas. The consumption rate is a system property: a direct-draw system at 12 to 14 psi runs near one pound of CO2 per half barrel, while a long-draw system pushing 30 to 40 psi through a glycol trunk uses considerably more, and a blended gas changes the arithmetic again. The practically useful output is the change-out point rather than the theoretical end, because a cylinder run to empty loses regulator pressure without warning and the next pour goes flat. Setting a reserve turns the calculation into a delivery schedule, and it usually shows that a single cylinder is a weekly item rather than a phone call. A cylinder scale and the supplier's measured consumption govern.

assumptions.name: Per-keg consumption
assumptions.value: near 1 lb per half barrel direct-draw at 12 to 14 psi; considerably more on a long-draw system at 30 to 40 psi
assumptions.source: Brewers Association Draught Beer Quality Manual

assumptions.name: Reserve
assumptions.value: a cylinder run to empty loses regulator pressure without warning, so the change-out is set short of the theoretical end

assumptions.name: Scales with volume
assumptions.value: consumption tracks the volume dispensed, not the number of taps

drying-goal.formula: Target indoor GPP = outdoor GPP - drying-gradient. IICRC S500-2021 'normal-drying' guidance: target 5-15 GPP below outdoor; psychrometric chart drives the dry-bulb / RH set point that delivers the target.
drying-goal.edition: IICRC S500-2021 (Standard for Professional Water Damage Restoration) by name.
drying-goal.freeAccess: IICRC standards licensed; principles free in published water-damage-restoration training literature.
drying-goal.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.

assumptions.name: Drying gradient
assumptions.value: 5-15 GPP below outdoor (S500 normal-drying band) unless user supplies

aerial-ladder.formula: Horizontal reach = ladder_length × cos(angle); vertical reach = ladder_length × sin(angle), measured from the turntable pivot; a manufacturer's rated vertical reach adds the pivot height above grade (Spartan's 75 ft rear mount prints 75 ft vertical where 75 x sin 72 is 71.3), so add it for the height above the street.
aerial-ladder.edition: NFPA 1901 (Standard for Automotive Fire Apparatus) by name; manufacturer aerial-device technical data sheets (Pierce, E-One, Sutphen) by name.
aerial-ladder.freeAccess: NFPA 1901 read-only at nfpa.org/freeaccess; manufacturer specs free on each manufacturer site.
aerial-ladder.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed fire protection engineer govern.

cash-conversion-cycle.formula: CCC = DIO + DSO - DPO. DIO = avg_inventory / (COGS / period_days). DSO = AR / (revenue / period_days). DPO = AP / (COGS / period_days).
cash-conversion-cycle.edition: Standard working-capital identity. First principles; user supplies the three day-counts.
cash-conversion-cycle.governance: Estimate. Verify before sending to your bookkeeper, banker, or CPA.

assumptions.name: Inputs
assumptions.value: user supplies DSO / DIO / DPO already computed
assumptions.source: tile is the cycle calculation, not the underlying ratios

clausius-clapeyron.formula: ln(P2/P1) = -(dHvap/R)(1/T2 - 1/T1), so dHvap = R ln(P2/P1) / (1/T1 - 1/T2); R = 8.314 J/(mol*K), T in kelvin. Only the pressure ratio enters. Slope of ln(P) vs 1/T is -dHvap/R.
clausius-clapeyron.edition: The Clausius-Clapeyron equation; standard physical chemistry / thermodynamics. First principles.
clausius-clapeyron.freeAccess: The Clausius-Clapeyron equation and the gas constant R are public first-principles chemistry; the vapor pressures and temperatures are the user's own measurements.
clausius-clapeyron.governance: Verify protocol against your lab's SOP before pipetting. A miscalculated dilution can ruin a run or a sample.
clausius-clapeyron.editionNote: The molar enthalpy of vaporization from two vapor-pressure/temperature points, the phase-equilibrium member the lab phys-chem set (ideal gas, Arrhenius, Nernst) leaves out. Because only the pressure ratio P2/P1 enters, any consistent unit (kPa, mmHg, atm, psi) gives the same enthalpy. Water from 760 mmHg at 100 C to 525.9 mmHg at 90 C returns about 41.5 kJ/mol against the tabulated 40.7; the small excess is the constant-enthalpy, ideal-vapor, negligible-liquid-volume approximation over the interval. The slope of a ln(P) vs 1/T plot is -dHvap/R. Apply the same equation with the enthalpy found here to predict a vapor pressure at a third temperature or a boiling point at a new pressure. A first-principles chemistry aid; the measured data govern.

assumptions.name: Clausius-Clapeyron
assumptions.value: dHvap = R ln(P2/P1)/(1/T1 - 1/T2), T in kelvin

assumptions.name: Unit-agnostic
assumptions.value: only the pressure ratio enters; P1 and P2 may be in any consistent unit

assumptions.name: Scope
assumptions.value: assumes constant dHvap and an ideal vapor over the interval (a curved ln(P) vs 1/T signals variation)

section-121-exclusion.formula: amount_realized = sale_price - selling_costs. adjusted_basis = purchase_price + capital_improvements. realized_gain = amount_realized - adjusted_basis. exclusion = min(realized_gain, cap) when the two-of-five test is met. cap = $250,000 single / $500,000 MFJ. taxable_gain = max(0, realized_gain - exclusion).
section-121-exclusion.edition: 26 USC 121 (Internal Revenue Code §121). Cap last amended by TRA-1997; non-qualified-use reduction added by HERA-2008 (effective 2009).
section-121-exclusion.freeAccess: 26 USC free at uscode.house.gov. IRS Pub 523 (Selling Your Home) free at irs.gov.
section-121-exclusion.governance: Estimate. Lender governs final underwriting and rate / fee disclosure. Appraiser governs the appraised value. State law and the agency's program guidelines may impose stricter limits than the published thresholds.
section-121-exclusion.editionNote: The two-of-five-year ownership and use test (§121(a)) is required for the full exclusion. Partial exclusion is available via §121(c) for unforeseen circumstances (job change > 50 miles, health, death, divorce). Non-qualified-use (rental after 2008) reduces the exclusion pro-rata per §121(b)(5).

assumptions.name: Filing-status caps
assumptions.value: single / MFS / HoH = $250,000; MFJ = $500,000

assumptions.name: Selling costs
assumptions.value: treated as a reduction to amount realized (vs. an addition to basis)

assumptions.name: Capital improvements
assumptions.value: user enters the total of basis-eligible improvements
assumptions.source: user attests; IRS Pub 530 covers what qualifies

joist-hanger-count.formula: joists = ceil(run_width_ft x 12 / spacing_in) + 1; hangers = joists x ends_per_joist; hanger_nails = hangers x nails_per_hanger.
joist-hanger-count.edition: Joist-hanger count identity by name (joists across the run, hangers on the hung ends, filled holes); first-principles count arithmetic.
joist-hanger-count.freeAccess: The count arithmetic is public first-principles; the hanger model and nailing come from the connector manufacturer.
joist-hanger-count.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
joist-hanger-count.editionNote: A hanger goes on each joist end that lands in a ledger or beam face; a joist bearing on top of a beam needs no hanger that end (set ends to 1). Every hanger hole is filled with the specified structural connector nails or screws (not roofing nails). The hanger model follows the manufacturer for the joist size and load.

assumptions.name: Hung ends
assumptions.value: 2 for a joist hung both ends; 1 if one end bears on a beam

assumptions.name: Nails per hanger
assumptions.value: ~10 filled holes with structural connector nails (default); the manufacturer's schedule governs

pv-ballast-weight.formula: total_wt_lb = modules x (module_wt_lb + ballast_per_module_lb) + racking_wt_lb; added_psf = total_wt_lb / array_area_sf; pass = added_psf <= allowable_psf.
pv-ballast-weight.edition: PV ballast load-screen identity by name (total dead load over the array footprint, screened against the allowable); first-principles arithmetic.
pv-ballast-weight.freeAccess: The load arithmetic is public first-principles; the ballast quantity and allowable pressure come from the PE-stamped ballast plan and the structural engineer.
pv-ballast-weight.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
pv-ballast-weight.editionNote: This is a dead-load SCREEN, not a design. The ballast quantity per module and the allowable roof pressure come from the PE-stamped ballast plan and the structural engineer (entered here); it totals and distributes the given ballast rather than sizing it. Wind uplift and the roof structure govern. A value over the allowable means re-check with the engineer.

assumptions.name: Ballast quantity
assumptions.value: per module from the PE-stamped ballast plan (entered); not sized here

assumptions.name: Allowable pressure
assumptions.value: the allowable added dead load from the structural engineer (entered)

haul-road-resistance.formula: total_resistance_pct = grade_pct + rolling_resistance_pct; required_rimpull_lb = total_resistance_pct / 100 x gvw_lb; rimpull_per_ton_lb = 20 x total_resistance_pct.
haul-road-resistance.edition: Haul-road resistance identity by name (total = grade + rolling; rimpull = total x GVW; 20 lb/ton per 1%); first-principles tractive-effort statics.
haul-road-resistance.freeAccess: The resistance statics are public first-principles; the available rimpull in gear comes from the manufacturer's rimpull-speed curve.
haul-road-resistance.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
haul-road-resistance.editionNote: Rolling resistance depends on the road surface - about 2% for a hard maintained haul road, 10% or more for soft or rutted ground. A downhill grade subtracts and can call for the retarder rather than rimpull. Compare the required rimpull to the machine's available rimpull in gear from the manufacturer's rimpull-speed curve; road maintenance is the cheapest way to cut it.

assumptions.name: Rolling resistance
assumptions.value: ~2% for a hard maintained haul road, 10%+ for soft or rutted ground (~4% default)

assumptions.name: Rimpull rule
assumptions.value: 20 lb/ton per 1% of total resistance; required rimpull = total resistance x GVW

welder-resistance-circuit-conductor.formula: duty_multiplier = the Table 630.31(A)(2) value at a listed duty cycle (50% 0.71, 40% 0.63, 30% 0.55, 25% 0.50, 20% 0.45, 15% 0.39, 10% 0.32, 7.5% 0.27, 5% or less 0.22), else sqrt(duty_pct / 100), the relation the table rounds; conductor_current_a = primary_current_a x duty_multiplier; ocpd_max_a = 3.0 x primary_current_a (630.32(A)).
welder-resistance-circuit-conductor.edition: NEC 630.31 (conductors) and 630.32 (overcurrent protection) for resistance welding equipment, by name; the welder nameplate and the adopted NEC edition govern.
welder-resistance-circuit-conductor.freeAccess: The duty-cycle conductor derating and the 300% OCPD limit are public NEC (many jurisdictions post the adopted NEC); the rated primary current and duty come from the welder nameplate.
welder-resistance-circuit-conductor.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
welder-resistance-circuit-conductor.editionNote: A resistance (spot / seam / projection) welder fires in brief, high-current pulses. NEC 630.31(A)(2) sizes the conductor for a specific nonrepetitive welder at the rated primary current times the Table 630.31(A)(2) multiplier: the printed two-place value at a listed duty (0.71 at 50%), the square root of the duty between rows, and 0.22 at 5% or less -- the same duty derating as an arc welder, because the brief pulses heat the conductor far less than the peak current would suggest. NEC 630.32(A) then permits the overcurrent device up to 300% of the rated primary current, HIGHER than the 200% allowed for arc welders (630.12), so the inrush of the weld pulses does not nuisance-trip the device. This is the resistance-welder method; arc welders (transformer / rectifier / motor-generator) use the separate 630.11 / 630.12 (200%) method. Use the welder's rated primary current and duty cycle; the AHJ, the welder nameplate, and the adopted NEC edition govern.

assumptions.name: Duty multiplier
assumptions.value: conductor at I_primary x the Table 630.31(A)(2) value at a listed duty, sqrt(duty) between rows, 0.22 at 5% or less, for a specific nonrepetitive welder

assumptions.name: OCPD 300%
assumptions.value: resistance-welder overcurrent device up to 300% of the rated primary (630.32(A)); arc welders are 200%

duct-hanger-load.formula: load_per_hanger_lb = duct_lb_per_ft x spacing_ft; count = ceil(run_ft / spacing_ft) + 1; utilization = load_per_hanger_lb / hanger_swl_lb.
duct-hanger-load.edition: Duct-hanger load / count identity by name (tributary weight per hanger; count from run and spacing); first-principles statics.
duct-hanger-load.freeAccess: The tributary-load statics are public first-principles; the max spacing (SMACNA) and hanger SWL come from SMACNA and the manufacturer.
duct-hanger-load.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
duct-hanger-load.editionNote: The maximum spacing follows SMACNA (about 8-10 ft for rectangular duct). The per-foot weight comes from duct-metal-weight, plus wrap and any water in a coil. The hanger, rod, or strap safe working load is the manufacturer's. Large duct goes on a trapeze.

assumptions.name: Max spacing
assumptions.value: ~8-10 ft for rectangular duct per SMACNA; entered here

assumptions.name: Per-foot weight
assumptions.value: from duct-metal-weight, plus wrap and any water in a coil

membrane-roof-takeoff.formula: usable_w_ft = roll_width_ft - sidelap_in/12; rolls = ceil(roof_area_sf x (1 + waste_pct/100) / (usable_w_ft x roll_length_ft)); seam_lf = roof_area_sf / usable_w_ft.
membrane-roof-takeoff.edition: Single-ply membrane takeoff identity by name (usable width nets the side lap; rolls from area / usable coverage; seam from area / usable width); first-principles takeoff arithmetic.
membrane-roof-takeoff.freeAccess: The membrane takeoff is public quantity geometry; the membrane and lap come from the manufacturer and the wind-uplift design.
membrane-roof-takeoff.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
membrane-roof-takeoff.editionNote: The usable width nets out the side lap. The seam length sizes the hot-air welding or adhesive and the labor. Fasteners, plates, and cover tape are taken off separately. The membrane and lap are set by the manufacturer and the wind-uplift design.

assumptions.name: Usable width
assumptions.value: roll width minus the side lap (a 10 ft roll with a 6 in lap nets 9.5 ft)

assumptions.name: Side lap
assumptions.value: set by the manufacturer and the wind-uplift design (~6 in typical)

sfrm-takeoff.formula: volume_ft3 = area_sf x thickness_in / 12; weight_lb = volume_ft3 x density_pcf; bags = ceil(weight_lb / bag_lb x (1 + waste_pct/100)).
sfrm-takeoff.edition: SFRM material-takeoff identity by name (in-place volume x density gives the weight; bags from weight and waste); first-principles takeoff arithmetic.
sfrm-takeoff.freeAccess: The takeoff arithmetic is public quantity geometry; the design thickness comes from the UL/ULC assembly (no rating table reproduced).
sfrm-takeoff.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
sfrm-takeoff.editionNote: The design thickness comes from the UL/ULC assembly for the required hourly rating; the density comes from the product. SFRM carries high in-place waste from overspray and rebound (~15%+). The design thickness, set by the fire rating, drives the whole order. Distinct from the wood char-depth-capacity.

assumptions.name: Design thickness
assumptions.value: from the UL/ULC assembly for the required hourly rating (varies by member size)

assumptions.name: Waste
assumptions.value: ~15%+ in-place from overspray and rebound; higher than most material takeoffs

flat-oval-duct.formula: A = (pi/4) b^2 + b (a - b); P = pi b + 2 (a - b); De = 1.55 A^0.625 / P^0.25 (a = major axis, b = minor axis). Equal-friction equivalent round diameter.
flat-oval-duct.edition: The ASHRAE equal-friction equivalent round diameter of a flat-oval duct, De = 1.55 A^0.625 / P^0.25, per ASHRAE Fundamentals (duct design) and SMACNA, by name; first-principles.
flat-oval-duct.freeAccess: First-principles equal-friction equivalence (not equal-velocity); the flat-oval area and perimeter are standard geometry. The fabrication drawing governs.
flat-oval-duct.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed mechanical contractor govern. ACCA Manual J / D / S supersede rules of thumb.
flat-oval-duct.editionNote: The flat-oval companion to the round-to-rect-duct tile. A flat oval is a rectangle of width (a - b) capped by two semicircles of diameter b, so its area is A = (pi/4) b^2 + b (a - b) and its perimeter P = pi b + 2 (a - b); the ASHRAE equal-friction equivalent round diameter is De = 1.55 A^0.625 / P^0.25. A 20 x 10 in flat oval carries air like a 14.8 in round, slightly under the 15.1 in equal-area round because the flatter shape has more rubbing surface per unit area; at a = b the shape is a round of diameter b. Equal-friction, not equal-velocity - size the round for friction and the flat oval for the space. Pairs with duct-sizing and round-to-rect-duct. A design aid; the duct-design method and the fabrication drawing govern.

assumptions.name: Equivalence basis
assumptions.value: equal friction, not equal velocity; De = 1.55 A^0.625 / P^0.25

assumptions.name: Flat-oval geometry
assumptions.value: A = (pi/4) b^2 + b (a - b); P = pi b + 2 (a - b), a = major, b = minor

weld-dilution.formula: dilution = A_base / (A_base + A_filler) x 100; filler_share = 100 - dilution.
weld-dilution.edition: The standard welding-metallurgy weld-dilution definition, by name.
weld-dilution.freeAccess: Weld dilution is a standard welding-metallurgy term defined in AWS references and filler-metal literature. The WPS and the filler-metal data govern.
weld-dilution.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
weld-dilution.editionNote: Weld dilution = melted base-metal area / total deposit area, the fraction of the weld that is base metal rather than filler. It sets how much the base metal's chemistry shifts the deposit: a structural single-pass weld runs 30-40%, but a hardfacing or corrosion overlay is kept low (weave, buttering, lower current) so the overlay chemistry stays near the filler's. This is the cross-sectional area ratio: it uses the entered melted and reinforcement areas (from a macro-etch or estimate) and does not itself compute the diluted alloy composition (that needs each metal's chemistry). A process aid; the WPS and the filler-metal data govern.

assumptions.name: Definition
assumptions.value: dilution = A_base / (A_base + A_filler)

assumptions.name: Overlay goal
assumptions.value: hardfacing/corrosion overlays kept low-dilution to preserve the filler chemistry

assumptions.name: Area ratio only
assumptions.value: uses entered areas; does not compute the diluted alloy composition

regular-polygon.formula: interior angle = (n-2)180/n; apothem = s/(2 tan(pi/n)); circumradius = s/(2 sin(pi/n)); across-flats = 2 apothem; across-corners = 2 circumradius; area = n s^2/(4 tan(pi/n)).
regular-polygon.edition: The regular-polygon relations (apothem, circumradius, across-flats/corners, area) - standard plane geometry as in Machinery's Handbook (Industrial Press), by name; public domain.
regular-polygon.freeAccess: Pure plane geometry, public; the side count and side length are user-supplied.
regular-polygon.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
regular-polygon.editionNote: Geometry of a regular (equal-sided, equal-angled) convex polygon of n sides and side length s. The interior angle is (n-2)180/n; the apothem (center to the middle of a side, the inradius of the circle that just touches each side) is a = s/(2 tan(pi/n)); the circumradius (center to a corner) is R = s/(2 sin(pi/n)); the across-flats is 2a (the wrench size of a nut or the width of hex stock) and the across-corners is 2R (the diagonal); the perimeter is n s and the area is n s^2/(4 tan(pi/n)) = (1/2)(perimeter)(apothem). Use it to cut hex or octagon stock, lay out a polygonal frame or tank footprint, or check a wrench opening. Irregular polygons, the miter/bevel to cut it (polygon-miter), and a bolt pattern on it (bolt-circle) are separate. Plane figures only. A shop and layout aid; verify critical dimensions on the work.

assumptions.name: Apothem / circumradius
assumptions.value: a = s/(2 tan(pi/n)), R = s/(2 sin(pi/n)); across-flats = 2a, across-corners = 2R

assumptions.name: Area
assumptions.value: n s^2/(4 tan(pi/n)) = (1/2)(perimeter)(apothem)

assumptions.name: Scope
assumptions.value: regular convex polygons; irregular shapes, miter, and bolt patterns are separate

wireless-link-budget.formula: EIRP = Pt + Gt - Lcable(tx); FSPL = 32.44 + 20 log10(d_km) + 20 log10(f_MHz); Prx = EIRP - FSPL + Gr - Lcable(rx); fade margin = Prx - Rx sensitivity. All in dB; target margin >= 10 dB.
wireless-link-budget.edition: The point-to-point wireless link budget - EIRP, free-space path loss, and fade margin - from the Friis transmission equation / ITU-R P.525, by name; first-principles dB accounting.
wireless-link-budget.freeAccess: The link-budget dB accounting and the Friis / FSPL relation are public first-principles RF (ITU-R P.525 is a free ITU download); the powers, gains, cable losses, distance, frequency, and receiver sensitivity are the user's link inputs.
wireless-link-budget.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed electrician govern. Verify against the NEC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
wireless-link-budget.editionNote: The full point-to-point wireless link budget, the RF endpoint that consumes free-space path loss the way fiber-loss-budget totals an optical channel. EIRP = Pt + Gt - Lcable(tx) leaves the transmit antenna; FSPL = 32.44 + 20 log10(d_km) + 20 log10(f_MHz) is subtracted over the path; the receive gain is added and receive cable loss subtracted for Prx = EIRP - FSPL + Gr - Lcable(rx); the fade margin = Prx - the receiver's sensitivity is the headroom against rain, multipath, and misalignment. A 20 dBm radio with 12 dBi antennas and 1 dB of cable each end over a 1 km 2.4 GHz path into a -80 dBm receiver delivers -58 dBm for a 22 dB fade margin. Aim for at least 10 dB of fade margin (20+ dB for a carrier-class or long/rainy link); a margin near zero or negative will not hold up. Free space only - atmospheric and rain attenuation (significant above ~10 GHz), obstruction and Fresnel-zone diffraction, and interference are separate. A planning estimate; the path survey, spectrum, and a commissioning test govern.

assumptions.name: Link budget
assumptions.value: EIRP = Pt + Gt - Lcable(tx); Prx = EIRP - FSPL + Gr - Lcable(rx); fade margin = Prx - sensitivity

assumptions.name: Target margin
assumptions.value: aim for >= 10 dB fade margin (20+ for carrier-class); free space only, rain/obstruction/interference separate

powered-attic-ventilator.formula: fan_cfm = attic_area x cfm_per_ft2 x (dark_roof ? 1.15 : 1.0); intake_ft2 = fan_cfm / 300; intake_in2 = intake_ft2 x 144. Default cfm_per_ft2 = 0.7.
powered-attic-ventilator.edition: Powered attic-ventilator sizing, standard roofing / attic-fan manufacturer practice (~0.7 CFM per ft^2, ~1 ft^2 intake per 300 CFM) by name; first-principles airflow.
powered-attic-ventilator.freeAccess: The CFM-per-square-foot and intake-per-CFM rules of thumb are published free in attic-fan manufacturer sizing guides.
powered-attic-ventilator.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
powered-attic-ventilator.editionNote: A powered attic ventilator (attic fan) is sized to roughly 0.7 CFM per square foot of attic floor (about 10 air changes per hour for a typical attic), increased by about 15% for a dark roof that runs hotter. The fan must be paired with adequate intake (soffit) net free area, roughly 1 square foot per 300 CFM, so it draws outdoor air rather than starving and depressurizing the attic (which can back-draft atmospheric combustion appliances or pull air-conditioned air out of the house through ceiling leaks). Powered fans are only one approach: balanced passive ridge-and-soffit ventilation (see attic-ventilation) is frequently preferred, and some codes and utility programs discourage or restrict powered attic fans on conditioned homes. A sizing aid; the fan manufacturer's data, the intake actually available, and the local code govern.

assumptions.name: Fan airflow
assumptions.value: ~0.7 CFM per ft^2 of attic floor (~10 ACH), +~15% for a dark roof

assumptions.name: Intake area
assumptions.value: ~1 ft^2 of net free intake per 300 CFM so the fan is not starved

assumptions.name: Passive preferred
assumptions.value: balanced passive ventilation is often preferred; some codes restrict powered fans

turnout-frog-lead.formula: frog angle F = 2 arctan(1 / (2 N)) (frog number N = 1/2 cot(F/2)), about 1 / N in radians; separation beyond the frog = track gauge (4 ft 8-1/2 in, the centerline offset at the theoretical point of frog) + distance / N; clearance point = (required separation - gauge) x N; track consumed from the point of switch = entered lead + clearance point.
turnout-frog-lead.edition: The frog-number geometry relations, by name, with 49 CFR 213 and the railroad's standard plans named. Lead, switch point length, closure curve radius, and the other layout dimensions come from the standard plan for the specific turnout and are entered, not computed. The track owner governs.
turnout-frog-lead.freeAccess: Trigonometry on a frog number the user states; no railroad standard plan or turnout dimension table is reproduced.
turnout-frog-lead.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
turnout-frog-lead.editionNote: The frog number is a slope: a number 10 frog spreads one unit sideways for every ten units along, which makes the angle a shade under six degrees. Higher numbers are flatter, faster, and longer, and that length is the practical constraint -- a number 20 turnout is a great deal of track, which is why yards use low numbers and main line crossovers use high ones. The number a track crew actually needs on the ground is the separation at a distance: how far from the frog do the two tracks stand apart by a given amount. That is what locates the clearance point, which is where a car may stand on the diverging track without fouling the main, and getting it wrong is how a car gets sideswiped. The approximate rule -- separation grows by about one over the frog number per foot beyond the frog -- is good enough to find it with a tape. Lead and the other layout dimensions come from the railroad's standard plan for that turnout and are not computed here; they depend on switch point length, closure curve, and the specific design, and no formula substitutes for the plan. The separation relation is a straight-line approximation that ignores the closure curve, which is adequate for locating a clearance point with a tape but not for design.

assumptions.name: Frog number is a slope
assumptions.value: one unit sideways for every N units along; higher is flatter, faster, and much longer

assumptions.name: The clearance point is the field question
assumptions.value: where a car may stand on the diverging track without fouling the main

assumptions.name: Lead comes from the standard plan
assumptions.value: switch point length, closure curve, and frog dimensions are design data, not a formula

uv-dose.formula: dose_mj_cm2 = intensity_mw_cm2 x exposure_time_s (mW.s/cm^2 = mJ/cm^2); meets the target if dose >= target_dose (default 40 mJ/cm^2), else short.
uv-dose.edition: USEPA UV Disinfection Guidance Manual (EPA 815-R-06-007) by name; dose = intensity x time, no edition cycle.
uv-dose.freeAccess: The dose relation is public; the validated reactor dose and the state primacy agency govern compliance.
uv-dose.governance: Estimate. Operator of record and primacy agency govern.
uv-dose.editionNote: Single-edition (the dose = intensity x time relation does not roll; the validated reactor dose and the state primacy agency govern compliance).

assumptions.name: Units
assumptions.value: mW.s/cm^2 equals mJ/cm^2; dose is the time integral of intensity, here intensity x time

assumptions.name: Target
assumptions.value: a common validated target is 40 mJ/cm^2, editable to the validated reactor dose

assumptions.name: Short dose
assumptions.value: a short dose points to an aged lamp, a fouled sleeve, or low UV transmittance (turbidity)

uv-required-exposure.formula: required_time_s = target_dose_mj_cm2 / intensity_mw_cm2; or required_intensity_mw_cm2 = target_dose_mj_cm2 / exposure_time_s (mW.s/cm^2 = mJ/cm^2).
uv-required-exposure.edition: USEPA UV Disinfection Guidance Manual (EPA 815-R-06-007) by name, the inverse of dose = intensity x time; no edition cycle.
uv-required-exposure.freeAccess: The dose relation is public; the validated reactor dose and the state primacy agency govern compliance.
uv-required-exposure.governance: Estimate. Operator of record and primacy agency govern.
uv-required-exposure.editionNote: The inverse of the UV-dose tile: from a target dose, solve the operand that is missing. Leave the intensity blank for the required contact time = dose / intensity, or leave the time blank for the required intensity = dose / time (mW.s/cm^2 = mJ/cm^2). A common validated target is 40 mJ/cm^2, editable to the validated reactor value. This answers how long a lamp of a known intensity must expose the flow, or how strong a lamp must be for a fixed contact time, to reach the target dose. A short delivered dose in service points to an aged lamp, a fouled sleeve, or low UV transmittance. Single-edition (the dose relation does not roll); the validated reactor dose and the state primacy agency govern compliance.

assumptions.name: Inverse relation
assumptions.value: time = dose / intensity, or intensity = dose / time; mW.s/cm^2 equals mJ/cm^2

assumptions.name: Target
assumptions.value: a common validated target is 40 mJ/cm^2, editable to the validated reactor dose

assumptions.name: One unknown
assumptions.value: enter exactly one of intensity or time; the tile solves for the other

pv-row-spacing.formula: rise = L x sin(tilt); base = L x cos(tilt); shadow = rise / tan(profile_angle); pitch = base + shadow; gap = shadow; gcr = L / pitch.
pv-row-spacing.edition: NREL / Sandia PV array row-spacing geometry (pitch = L x cos(tilt) + L x sin(tilt) / tan(profile_angle), GCR = L / pitch), by name; the relations are first-principles trigonometry.
pv-row-spacing.freeAccess: The row-spacing geometry and the ground-coverage-ratio definition are public NREL / Sandia relations and first-principles trigonometry.
pv-row-spacing.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
pv-row-spacing.editionNote: The NREL / Sandia PV array row-spacing geometry pitch = L x cos(tilt) + L x sin(tilt) / tan(profile_angle), GCR = L / pitch. The minimum solar profile angle is the winter-design sun elevation at the site (commonly the solar altitude at 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. on the winter solstice, read from the latitude or from solar-times); the relation assumes due-south rows and a level field (an azimuth offset or a graded slope is a separate correction). The no-shadow layout geometry, not an annual inter-row shading-loss model.

assumptions.name: Row pitch
assumptions.value: pitch = collector horizontal footprint + the shadow its top edge throws at the minimum profile angle

assumptions.name: Profile angle
assumptions.value: the winter-design sun elevation; a profile angle near the horizon throws an effectively infinite shadow

assumptions.name: Ground-coverage ratio
assumptions.value: GCR = collector length / pitch drives both the land area and the inter-row shading

distance-distance-intersection.formula: d = |P1-P0|; a = (r0^2 - r1^2 + d^2)/(2d); h = sqrt(r0^2 - a^2); Pm = P0 + a*(P1-P0)/d; solutions = Pm +/- h*(perpendicular unit). Real iff |r0-r1| <= d <= r0+r1.
distance-distance-intersection.edition: First-principles Euclidean geometry (two-circle / trilateration intersection), the standard swing-tie locate as compiled in the route-surveying references (Ghilani & Wolf, Elementary Surveying), by name.
distance-distance-intersection.freeAccess: The two-circle intersection is public first-principles geometry; the control coordinates and the two measured distances are the user's field data.
distance-distance-intersection.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
distance-distance-intersection.editionNote: The distance-distance (swing-tie) intersection: the coordinates of a point located by measuring its distance to two known control points, the tape method behind an as-built tie, a batter-board corner, or a two-tape locate. It is where two circles cross - one of radius r0 about control point 1, one of radius r1 about control point 2. With the points d apart, the foot of the crossing chord is a = (r0^2 - r1^2 + d^2)/(2d) from point 1 and the two crossings are h = sqrt(r0^2 - a^2) to each side, so there are two mirror-image solutions across the line between the control points; the field sketch or a rough third tie tells which side. A real solution exists only when |r0 - r1| <= d <= r0 + r1: if d > r0 + r1 the distances are too short to meet, and if d < |r0 - r1| one circle lies inside the other - both flagged, as is the tangent (single-solution) case. Coordinates are plane northing/easting on the project grid (flat-plane geometry; grid scale factor and elevation are separate). A computational aid; the project control and datum govern.

assumptions.name: Two-circle intersection
assumptions.value: a = (r0^2 - r1^2 + d^2)/(2d), h = sqrt(r0^2 - a^2); solutions = midpoint +/- h*perpendicular

assumptions.name: Two solutions
assumptions.value: mirror images across the control line; the field sketch or a third tie resolves the side

assumptions.name: Plane geometry
assumptions.value: plane grid northing/easting; grid scale factor and elevation are separate

accessible-toilet-compartment.formula: wheelchair accessible compartment: width >= 60 in; depth >= 56 in for a wall hung water closet or >= 59 in for a floor mounted one. Ambulatory accessible compartment: depth >= 60 in and 35 in <= width <= 37 in. An ambulatory compartment is required in addition where compartments >= 6 OR (urinals + water closets) >= 6.
accessible-toilet-compartment.edition: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design, 213.3.1, 604.8.1.1, and 604.8.2.1. A US federal standard in the public domain, quoted directly.
accessible-toilet-compartment.freeAccess: The 2010 ADA Standards are published in full at no cost at ada.gov and by the US Access Board.
accessible-toilet-compartment.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
accessible-toilet-compartment.editionNote: Two compartments can be owed and the second is triggered by an OR that gets read as an AND. Section 213.3.1 requires one wheelchair accessible compartment wherever toilet compartments are provided, and one ambulatory accessible compartment IN ADDITION where six or more toilet compartments are provided or where the combination of urinals and water closets totals six or more fixtures. A room with four stalls and three urinals is seven fixtures and owes an ambulatory compartment even though nobody counted six stalls - the case that gets missed, because the stalls get counted and the urinals do not. In addition means in addition: one large accessible stall among five ordinary ones does not satisfy both. The wheelchair compartment depth follows the FIXTURE, not the partition layout: 56 in for a wall hung water closet and 59 in for a floor mounted one, so substituting one for the other can fail a compartment without moving anything, and a 56 in stall that was fine on the drawings fails when the specified wall carrier is value-engineered out. The ambulatory compartment width is a WINDOW rather than a minimum - 35 in minimum and 37 in MAXIMUM - so a 40 in stall is too wide to qualify. Too wide is a genuine failure rather than a bonus, because the compartment exists to put grab bars on both side walls within reach of someone who walks but needs support, and a generous stall defeats the purpose. Not checked: door swing and the requirement that a compartment door not swing into the minimum required area, door opening width and location; toe clearance under the front and side partitions and the exception that applies at greater depths; grab bar length, height, and position; water closet centerline location; clear floor space and turning space in the room itself; lavatory, dispenser, and mirror requirements; the accessible route to the room; children's-use dimensions, which differ; and the additional requirements of ANSI A117.1, the adopted building code, and state and local accessibility law. A compartment sizing screen, not a restroom design.

assumptions.name: Wheelchair compartment width
assumptions.value: 60 in minimum, measured perpendicular to the side wall

assumptions.name: Wheelchair compartment depth
assumptions.value: 56 in minimum for wall hung, 59 in minimum for floor mounted water closets

assumptions.name: Ambulatory compartment
assumptions.value: 60 in deep minimum, 35 in minimum to 37 in maximum wide

assumptions.name: Ambulatory trigger
assumptions.value: six or more compartments, OR urinals plus water closets totalling six or more

assumptions.name: Ambulatory compartment
assumptions.value: required in addition to the wheelchair compartment, not as an alternative

rc-tbeam-flexure.formula: trial a = As fy / (0.85 f'c be); if a <= hf the section is rectangular of width be and Mn = As fy (d - a/2); if a > hf then Asf = 0.85 f'c (be - bw) hf / fy, Asw = As - Asf, a = Asw fy / (0.85 f'c bw), and Mn = Asf fy (d - hf/2) + Asw fy (d - a/2). c = a/beta1; eps_t = 0.003 (d - c)/c; phi = 0.90 at eps_t >= eps_ty + 0.003, 0.65 at eps_t <= eps_ty = fy/Es, interpolated between.
rc-tbeam-flexure.edition: ACI 318-19: 22.2.2.4.1 equivalent rectangular stress block, 22.2.2.4.3 beta1, 6.3.2 effective flange width (delegated to the landed t-beam-effective-flange-width tile rather than reimplemented), and 21.2.2 strength-reduction factor.
rc-tbeam-flexure.freeAccess: The T-beam flexural derivation is standard reinforced-concrete mechanics reproduced in every textbook and in free university course notes; the code sections are cited by number and no table is reproduced.
rc-tbeam-flexure.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
rc-tbeam-flexure.editionNote: The useful result is which of the two behaviors applies, because it is not obvious and it decides everything. For most positive-moment T-beams the compression block stays entirely inside the slab, and then the section is simply a wide rectangle - the web width does not enter the flexural answer at all, which surprises people who expect a T-beam to need T-beam math. Only when the steel is heavy enough to push the block past the flange does true T action appear, and then the overhanging flange carries its own couple at the longer lever arm d - hf/2 while the web carries the rest. Treating a true T as a plain rectangle of the effective width is UNCONSERVATIVE: the example section returns 872.9 kip-ft correctly against 881.6 as a rectangle, about 1% high, because the rectangle credits the overhang compression at too deep a centroid. The strength-reduction factor follows ACI 318-19 21.2.2, whose tension-controlled limit is eps_ty + 0.003 rather than the fixed 0.005 of the 2014 edition - the two coincide only near Grade 60 and diverge at Grade 80 and 100. POSITIVE MOMENT ONLY: over a support the slab is in tension, the flange contributes nothing, and the section reverts to a rectangle of the WEB width; using this tile there overstates the capacity badly. Singly reinforced - compression steel is the doubly-reinforced tile. Minimum steel (9.6.1.2), shear, deflection, bar spacing, and development are separate checks with their own tiles. A design aid, not a substitute for a licensed engineer's design; the engineer of record's stamped design governs.

assumptions.name: Behavior test
assumptions.value: trial a on width be against hf decides rectangular versus true T

assumptions.name: Flange couple
assumptions.value: Asf = 0.85 f'c (be - bw) hf / fy at lever arm d - hf/2

assumptions.name: Effective width
assumptions.value: delegated to computeTBeamEffectiveFlangeWidth (6.3.2), with an override

assumptions.name: phi
assumptions.value: 21.2.2, tension-controlled at eps_ty + 0.003, not the 318-14 fixed 0.005

assumptions.name: Positive moment only
assumptions.value: at a support the flange is in tension and the section is a web-width rectangle

assumptions.name: Singly reinforced
assumptions.value: compression steel, minimum steel, shear, deflection, and development are separate

disinfectant-dwell.formula: Reference lookup: product class -> label-typical wet contact (dwell) time range, keep-wet rule, pre-clean rule, and the FIFRA label authority. No numeric computation beyond the lookup.
disinfectant-dwell.edition: Antimicrobial contact-time principle, by name; ANSI/IICRC S500 and S520. Antimicrobials are EPA-registered pesticides whose label is the legal authority under FIFRA.
disinfectant-dwell.freeAccess: States the contact time the label requires and the keep-wet / pre-clean rules that decide whether a disinfection claim is actually achieved.
disinfectant-dwell.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
disinfectant-dwell.editionNote: Single-edition (the typical ranges are guidance; the specific EPA-registered product label GOVERNS the exact dwell under FIFRA). The surface must stay visibly wet for the full contact time (re-apply if it dries), and disinfection requires pre-cleaning because product cannot penetrate soil. ANSI/IICRC S500 and S520 name the remediation context.

assumptions.name: Label authority
assumptions.value: the EPA-registered product label is the legal authority (FIFRA); the ranges shown are guidance

assumptions.name: Keep-wet rule
assumptions.value: the surface must remain visibly wet for the full contact time

esp-deutsch-efficiency.formula: Deutsch: efficiency = 1 - exp(-A w / Q) with the flow on a per-second basis; the area a target needs is -ln(1 - target) x Q / w; and the area per factor of ten off the penetration is ln(10) x Q / w, the same for every decade.
esp-deutsch-efficiency.edition: The Deutsch equation for electrostatic precipitator collection. The migration velocity is ENTERED because it depends on particle size, field strength and above all dust RESISTIVITY, and in practice is fitted from the performance of a similar installation rather than predicted. A screening calculation: it does not model resistivity, back corona, gas conditioning, rapping re-entrainment, sneakage or gas distribution, and it does not size the fields, transformer-rectifier sets or hoppers.
esp-deutsch-efficiency.freeAccess: One exponential; no manufacturer data is reproduced.
esp-deutsch-efficiency.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
esp-deutsch-efficiency.editionNote: Each equal increment of plate area removes the same FRACTION of the remaining penetration rather than the same amount of dust, so efficiency approaches 100% asymptotically and going from 99 to 99.9% requires exactly as much additional plate as going from zero to 90% did. That is why high-efficiency precipitators are enormous and why the last increment is the expensive one. The migration velocity is the weak input: it is fitted backwards from a similar installation on a similar dust, so a Deutsch calculation is only as good as the velocity it was given. Resistivity is the dominant variable in real performance and cuts both ways -- too high and back corona destroys collection, too low and particles re-entrain.

assumptions.name: Migration velocity is entered
assumptions.value: it is fitted from performance, not predicted from first principles
assumptions.source: a similar installation on a similar dust

assumptions.name: Resistivity is not modelled
assumptions.value: it is the dominant variable and is managed by conditioning

assumptions.name: Rapping re-entrainment is not included
assumptions.value: measured efficiency commonly falls short of the Deutsch value

ups-module-redundancy.formula: IT kVA = IT kW/power factor; N = ceil(kVA/module rating); N+1 = N+1 modules; 2N = 2N modules; loss = IT(1/efficiency - 1).
ups-module-redundancy.edition: Standard N, N+1, and 2N availability conventions with first-principles UPS conversion-loss arithmetic. Manufacturer efficiency curves and facility availability requirements govern.
ups-module-redundancy.freeAccess: Ceilings, utilization ratios, and an input/output efficiency balance.
ups-module-redundancy.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
ups-module-redundancy.editionNote: Nameplate redundancy does not establish concurrent maintainability or fault isolation. UPS efficiency varies strongly with module loading; entered efficiencies must come from the selected topology's part-load curve.

assumptions.name: Balanced modules
assumptions.value: load shares equally among all online modules

assumptions.name: Cooling penalty
assumptions.value: UPS loss divided by the entered cooling COP

crac-sensible-derate.formula: sensible capacity = 1.08 x airflow x (return temperature - supply temperature); tons = Btu/hr/12,000.
crac-sensible-derate.edition: The ASHRAE air-side sensible-heat relation and computer-room cooling rating practice. Manufacturer performance data and ASHRAE TC 9.9 govern.
crac-sensible-derate.freeAccess: A public sensible-heat balance and unit conversions.
crac-sensible-derate.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
crac-sensible-derate.editionNote: Airflow alone is not capacity. Bypass air lowers return temperature and coil delta-T, while containment raises it; fan heat, latent load, altitude, coil approach, and compressor limits remain outside this screen.

assumptions.name: Air constant
assumptions.value: 1.08 at ordinary standard-air conditions

assumptions.name: Sensible-only model
assumptions.value: latent load and manufacturer operating-envelope limits excluded

instant-off-ir-drop.formula: IR drop = instant-off minus ON potential; -0.850 V criterion applied to the instant-off potential against Cu/CuSO4; polarisation = native minus instant-off.
instant-off-ir-drop.edition: NACE SP0169 (now AMPP) and the CP designer govern.
instant-off-ir-drop.freeAccess: The criteria are in NACE SP0169; public reference cells and interrupters make the measurement.
instant-off-ir-drop.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
instant-off-ir-drop.editionNote: The ON potential includes soil IR drop, which is not polarisation of the steel -- read against it, a thin real margin looks comfortable. One rectifier left running voids the instant-off reading.

assumptions.name: Reference electrode
assumptions.value: copper-copper sulfate; other references shift every figure

assumptions.name: Interruption
assumptions.value: every influencing source must be interrupted synchronously

assumptions.name: Where 100 mV does not apply
assumptions.value: not on bimetallic systems (mixed potentials) or under stray current; steel coupled to copper can clear 100 mV and still be unprotected
assumptions.source: UFC 3-570-06 (2019) 2-1.3.1; MPCA, Guidelines for the Evaluation of UST Cathodic Protection Systems (2012) p.14

mechanical-room-nc.formula: L_p2 = L_p1 - TL + 10 log10(S / A); the flanking test compares that calculated level against a measured one, and the gap in decibels is a factor of 10^(gap/10) in energy.
mechanical-room-nc.edition: Octave-band transmission loss is the right input. STC is weighted for SPEECH frequencies and mechanical noise is concentrated far lower, so an STC number is the wrong number here.
mechanical-room-nc.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
mechanical-room-nc.editionNote: THE FLANKING TEST IS THE POINT OF DOING THIS AT ALL. Neither the source level nor the transmission loss is known precisely in the field, so the absolute prediction carries real uncertainty -- but the DIFFERENCE between prediction and measurement is robust. If the wall should deliver 45 dB and the room reads 55, that is a factor of ten in energy and no wall built as specified underperforms by that much: there is a flanking path, and finding it is cheaper than any acoustic upgrade. If they agree, the wall is performing as built and the choice is a better wall, a quieter machine, or vibration isolation. FLANKING IS WHY UPGRADES DISAPPOINT -- a partition that stops at the ceiling grid over a shared plenum makes the wall's rating nearly irrelevant, and a few square inches of unsealed penetration can undo an entire assembly, which is why sealing is not a detail. AND STC DOES NOT DESCRIBE MECHANICAL NOISE: a high-STC wall can perform poorly against a chiller or a fan.

assumptions.name: Single band
assumptions.value: an NC rating needs the whole spectrum

assumptions.name: Airborne path only
assumptions.value: structure-borne transmission is separate and often dominant

assumptions.name: Transmission loss entered by band
assumptions.value: an STC number is the wrong input for a low-frequency source

first-flush-diverter.formula: diversion = roof footprint / 100 x rate (1 to 2 gal per 100 sq ft; minimum 10 gal per 1,000 sq ft); rain depth (in) = gallons x 231 / (footprint x 144); standpipe length per gallon (in) = 231 / (pi/4 x d^2); length = gallons x that.
first-flush-diverter.edition: Texas Water Development Board, The Texas Manual on Rainwater Harvesting, 3rd ed. (2005), Chapter 2, First-Flush Diverters (pp. 7-8), by name. The local health department (for potable use) and the AHJ govern.
first-flush-diverter.freeAccess: A free state manual's rule of thumb, restated; the standpipe length is cylinder geometry at 231 cubic inches per gallon.
first-flush-diverter.governance: Estimate. Operator of record and primacy agency govern.
first-flush-diverter.editionNote: The first flush carries what accumulated on the roof between rains, and after a storm or a fire that includes debris and ash. The TWDB range of 1 to 2 gallons per 100 sq ft is a rule of thumb, and the manual says no exact calculation exists; dry days, roof surface, overhang, and season move it. One gallon per 100 sq ft is the first sixtieth of an inch of rain, so diverting costs almost nothing in yield. A gallon fills 33 in of 3-inch pipe but 8 in of 6-inch, so a diverter built from whatever pipe is at hand can be short by a factor of four. The footprint is measured in plan, and each downspout gets its own diverter.

assumptions.name: Roof footprint in plan
assumptions.value: horizontal projection of the area draining to the downspout, not the sloped surface
assumptions.source: TWDB Texas Manual on Rainwater Harvesting

assumptions.name: Nominal pipe diameter
assumptions.value: as the manual uses; actual inside diameters differ by a few percent
assumptions.source: TWDB Texas Manual on Rainwater Harvesting

assumptions.name: Not a treatment step
assumptions.value: diverted rainwater still needs filtration and disinfection for potable use
assumptions.source: TWDB Texas Manual on Rainwater Harvesting

generator-altitude-temp-derate.formula: altitude derate % = rate per step x max(0, site elevation - threshold) / step; temperature derate % = rate per step x max(0, site ambient - threshold) / step; combined (added, conservative) = altitude % + temperature %; available kW = rated kW x (1 - combined %); the multiplied combination (1 - a)(1 - t) is shown beside it.
generator-altitude-temp-derate.edition: The generator manufacturer's published derate statement for the specific model and rating (worked example from the Cummins DQDAC data sheet: full output to 1,800 ft and 104 degF, 7% per 1,312 ft and 7% per 18 degF beyond), named as the method and as governing; NFPA 110 cited by number for the requirement that the EPSS be rated for its site conditions.
generator-altitude-temp-derate.freeAccess: Arithmetic on thresholds and rates the user enters from the unit's own data sheet; no manufacturer derate curve or code table is reproduced.
generator-altitude-temp-derate.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed electrician govern. Verify against the NEC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
generator-altitude-temp-derate.editionNote: A diesel engine makes power by burning air, and thin or hot air carries less of it, so every generator data sheet states full output up to an altitude and an ambient temperature and then a percentage off for each step beyond. The thresholds and rates differ by model, by rating (standby against prime), and by fuel -- roughly 3% to 7% per step -- so they are entered from the unit actually being used. Data sheets say the two derates must be combined when both thresholds are exceeded and rarely say how; adding them is the conservative reading and matches manufacturers that call the temperature derate additional, while multiplying the factors gives a slightly higher figure. The tile uses the added figure and shows both. The derate matters most where a unit sized at sea level is dispatched to a high, hot site, and the first symptom is a voltage dip or stall on a motor start.

assumptions.name: The unit's own derate rules
assumptions.value: thresholds, steps, and rates are entered from the data sheet for the model and rating in use

assumptions.name: Derates combined by addition
assumptions.value: the conservative reading of 'must be combined'; the multiplied figure is shown for comparison

assumptions.name: Site rating required
assumptions.value: the emergency power supply must be rated for the conditions at its site

flood-debris-impact.formula: Fi = W x V x C_D x C_B x C_Str at the still-water level; V default = 1/2 sqrt(g ds); C_D = 1.0 in a floodway or Zone V, else 0.25 (ds - 1) clamped to 0-1 (Table 8-3 rows); C_B = 1.0, 0.6, 0.2, 0.0 by upstream screening; C_Str = 0.2, 0.4, 0.8 s/ft by structure.
flood-debris-impact.edition: FEMA P-55, Coastal Construction Manual, Volume II, Chapter 8 -- Eq. 8.9, Tables 8-3 and 8-4, and the building structure coefficients; ASCE 7 Chapter C5 cited by number. The engineer of record governs.
flood-debris-impact.freeAccess: FEMA P-55 is a free federal publication; its coefficients are transcribed; ASCE 7 is cited by chapter only.
flood-debris-impact.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed structural engineer govern.
flood-debris-impact.editionNote: FEMA's debris equation turns an impulse into a force: a mass moving with the water, stopped by a structure whose stiffness sets how quickly it stops. A stiff reinforced concrete wall takes four times the force of a flexible timber pile from the same object because it stops it faster. The depth and blockage coefficients reduce the effect where shallow water or upstream screening slows the debris. The 1,000 lb default stands for a piece of a damaged building, a pole, a length of pile, or an empty tank where nothing better is known; log-debris coasts need a larger weight from local guidance. The force is concentrated at the still-water elevation, which is what an overturning or pile-bending check needs. The default velocity is Eq. 8.9's 1/2 sqrt(g ds), but FEMA's own Example 8.4 enters the upper bound, 12.2 ft/s at 4.6 ft, for an oceanfront building (2,440 lb on a timber pile, twice the default's force). This is the P-55 (2011) method; ASCE 7-22 Supplement 2 (FEMA P-2345, April 2024) moved debris impact to the ASCE 7-22 Chapter 6 approach.

assumptions.name: Debris weight
assumptions.value: 1,000 lb recommended where local debris is unknown

assumptions.name: Depth coefficient
assumptions.value: Table 8-3 rows (0 at 1 ft to 1.0 at 5 ft) on the line 0.25 (ds - 1)

assumptions.name: Structure coefficient
assumptions.value: 0.2 timber pile or masonry column, 0.4 concrete pile or moment frame, 0.8 reinforced concrete wall
